prerequisites.title: Owner role on developer account
prerequisites.detail: Only an owner can accept the Clover Developer Agreement and edit account settings.

prerequisites.title: Identity and business documents
prerequisites.detail: Have a passport or driver's license, proof of home address, and for companies an EIN/Tax ID plus proof of business address.

prerequisites.title: Composio auth config with your own credentials
prerequisites.detail: Clover has no managed app, so you supply your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create global developer account
steps.detail: Sign up and create a global developer account as an owner; accept the developer agreement.
steps.done_when: Account exists and agreement is accepted

steps.title: Submit production account for approval
steps.detail: Fill the identity section, choosing Individual or Business, with matching address and tax ID details.
inputs: EIN or Tax ID for companies

steps.title: Upload requested documents within deadline
steps.detail: If Clover emails a request, upload documents to the secure Clover Box within 10 business days. Never send them by email.

steps.title: Wait for account verification
steps.detail: Clover reviews and contacts you only if more information is needed. No timeline is documented.

steps.title: Create the app and set OAuth options
steps.detail: In the Developer Dashboard, create the app, set the Default OAuth Response to Code, and configure the OAuth flow URL.

steps.title: Draft permission reasons
steps.detail: Draft the reason text for requested permissions such as READ Merchant, and Ecommerce online payments if you use card-not-present tokens.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config with your Clover client ID and secret, using the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Submit app to App Market
steps.detail: Submit the approved-account app for listing, including legal URLs.

steps.title: Wait for DevRel review
steps.detail: DevRel approves or rejects. No timeline is documented.

traps.title: No documented review timeline
traps.detail: Clover gives no review times, and a developer reported 7 weeks of silence and unanswered support emails.

traps.title: AI apps may be rejected
traps.detail: One founder reported a rejection because Clover had no policy for third-party AI apps. Ask Clover DevRel early.

traps.title: Document deadline
traps.detail: Requested documents must arrive within 10 business days or the application may be rejected.

traps.title: Address documents must match
traps.detail: The home address must match a utility bill, bank statement or similar; a P.O. box is not valid for an individual.

traps.title: Public listing unavailable for external POS apps
traps.detail: External POS apps using the REST Pay API are not on the public App Market.

open_questions: Is a separate app review required for non-listed production apps? Ask Clover DevRel (developer-relations@devrel.clover.com).
How long does developer account approval take? Not documented; ask DevRel.
Does Clover accept third-party AI agent apps? Ask DevRel before investing in a listing.
Which OAuth scopes are sensitive? The docs list permissions, not scopes, and name none as triggering extra review.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: The Developer Dashboard is on the **legacy developer platform**. If you have previously approved apps on this platform, you can continue to use the Developer Dashboard to manage the apps.
evidence.answer: The Developer Dashboard is on the legacy developer platform, not the current one.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: If you have previously approved apps on this platform, you can continue to use the Developer Dashboard to manage the apps.
evidence.answer: Developers who previously had approved apps on the legacy platform can keep using the Developer Dashboard to manage those apps.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: All new developer accounts in North America, Europe, Latin America, and Asia Pacific are created on the [global developer platform](https://docs.clover.com/dev/docs/global-developer-platform-get-started).
evidence.answer: All new developer accounts in North America, Europe, Latin America, and Asia Pacific are created on the global developer platform.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: The developer platform requires two separate developer accounts to access the sandbox and production environments.
evidence.answer: The legacy developer platform requires two separate developer accounts, one for the sandbox and one for production.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Developer must have Owner role to view and edit account settings in Developer Settings—Account Info.
evidence.answer: Only a developer with the Owner role can view and edit account settings in Developer Settings—Account Info.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Approved developers can submit apps for the Clover App Market.
evidence.answer: Only approved developers can submit apps for the Clover App Market.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Clover must verify and approve your production developer account before starting the app approval process.
evidence.answer: Clover must verify and approve the production developer account before the app approval process starts.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Account approval is **not needed** if you intend to use only the sandbox environment.
evidence.answer: Account approval is not needed if the developer uses only the sandbox environment.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: You can submit your production developer account for approval while building and testing your app on the sandbox, but it is **not required**.
evidence.answer: Submitting the production account for approval while testing on the sandbox is optional, not required.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: After your account is approved, the status of your developer account on the Developer Settings page is updated to **Account Verified**.
evidence.answer: After approval, the developer account status on the Developer Settings page changes to Account Verified, and the developer receives an approval email.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Required. Information to verify the developer’s identity and to contact, if needed, for additional details.
evidence.answer: Identity verification is required to verify the developer's identity and to allow Clover to contact them for more details if needed.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: **OFAC check**—Clover must run an Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) check on every developer as part of the approval process.
evidence.answer: Clover must run an OFAC (Office of Foreign Assets Control) check on every developer as part of approval.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: **International developers**—If the developer’s address is outside the intended market, an unexpired passport is required.
evidence.answer: For international developers whose address is outside the intended market, an unexpired passport is required.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Developers in Canada and the United Kingdom (UK) can provide a current driver’s license instead of a passport.
evidence.answer: Developers in Canada and the United Kingdom can provide a current driver's license instead of a passport.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Employer identification number (EIN) or tax identifier (Tax ID) from a government tax authority-issued document.
evidence.answer: A business developer must provide an EIN or Tax ID from a government tax authority-issued document (9 alphanumeric characters).

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Developer’s home address, including street, city, 2-character state code, country, and postal or ZIP code as mentioned on a utility bill, bank statement, or other legal document matching the address of the developer account.
evidence.answer: The developer's home address must match a utility bill, bank statement, or other legal document; a P.O. box is valid for an organization but not for an individual representative.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If the [Clover App Market](https://www.clover.com/appmarket) business team needs to contact you for more information, they also share a secure Clover Box folder URL (link) with you.
evidence.answer: If Clover's business team needs more information, they share a secure Clover Box folder link for uploading required documentation.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Do not share any required identity documentation by email.
evidence.answer: Identity documentation must not be sent by email; it must be uploaded to the specified Clover Box folder.

evidence.question: G6

evidence.answer: After account approval, Clover repeats the OFAC check monthly.

evidence.question: G1

evidence.answer: Creating a production Clover app requires a production developer account, which must be approved first.

evidence.question: G2

evidence.answer: External POS apps using the REST Pay API are not listed on the public Clover App market, but they are visible to merchants using the integrated POS.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: To complete a payment on the Clover device, you must authorize your app to read merchant data from a Clover device.
evidence.answer: For card-present payments, the app must request READ permission for Merchant so it can read merchant data from the Clover device.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: In the reason field, enter Required to connect POS app to Clover device using REST Pay API .
evidence.answer: For card-present payments, the READ Merchant permission is requested with a reason text entered in the Reason field.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If your app lets merchants create and use ECOMM_COMPAT card tokens for card-not-present (CNP) transactions, you must also configure your app for the Ecommerce API.
evidence.answer: For card-not-present payments, the app must also enable the Ecommerce 'Enable online payments' option and set a reason for it, if it lets merchants create and use ECOMM_COMPAT card tokens.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: In the Ecommerce section, select the Enable online payments checkbox.
evidence.answer: The Ecommerce permission flow requires selecting the Enable online payments checkbox in the Ecommerce section of Requested Permissions.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: To integrate your point of sale (POS) with a production Clover device, you need to create a Clover app that merchants can install.
evidence.answer: The app is something merchants install, and merchants authorize it through OAuth 2.0.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When your merchant is authorized through OAuth 2.0, you receive an authorization code.
evidence.answer: When a merchant authorizes the app through OAuth 2.0, the developer receives an authorization code.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: The Site URL must be the link to the home page of the web app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Optionally, if you are integrating with Cloud Pay Display, enter a domain link (URL) in the CORS Domain field.
evidence.answer: An optional CORS Domain URL can be set, but only if integrating with Cloud Pay Display.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: When you set a CORS domain URL, your web app can make calls to the Clover REST API without requiring an intermediate app server.
evidence.answer: Setting a CORS domain URL lets the web app call the Clover REST API without an intermediate app server.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Log in to Developer Dashboard .
evidence.answer: To create the app, log in to the Developer Dashboard and click Create App.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Select one or more countries where you want to make your app available for Clover merchants.
evidence.answer: In the Create App window, enter an app name and select one or more countries where the app will be available for Clover merchants.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Click Create . The App name - App Settings page appears.
evidence.answer: Clicking Create opens the App Settings page for the app.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: For a semi-integrated POS app, set the app type under REST Clients to Web and answer Yes to whether it is an integration of an existing point of sale.

evidence.answer: After saving the app type, the App Settings page shows a Remote App ID (RAID) that identifies the semi-integrated app.
